# Product Categories

# Products: Managing Categories

Effective category management is essential for streamlining your Point of Sale (POS) navigation. Organizing products into logical groups allows for faster checkout and better inventory oversight.

---

## Getting Started
To begin managing your product structure, navigate to **Products** > **Manage Categories**. From this interface, you can build a multi-level hierarchy of categories and subcategories.

### Creating a Category
1. Click **New Category**.
2. **Name & Description:** Provide a clear title and an optional description.
3. **Visual Customization:** Select an icon and background color. 
    * *Note: These visual elements are specifically for POS display purposes.*
4. **Images:** After saving, you can upload a background image. 
    * **Recommendation:** Use **WebP** files to keep file sizes small and ensure the POS interface remains fast.
5. **Status:** Toggle the category as **Active** or **Inactive**.
6. **Save:** Click Save to finalize the entry.

![Product Categories](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/06ced33d-e6a3-42d6-80fd-d7ae5e28f513.png)

![Product Icons, Colors, and Category Images](https://nazkcvruighrhpgcarxg.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/help-documentation-images/5a9244e7-5ce9-4d47-89c0-47b277b0d205.png)

### Creating Subcategories
Subcategories follow the same creation process as parent categories. The only difference is that you must select a **Parent Category** from the dropdown menu to nest the new category underneath it. There is no limit to the number of subcategory levels you can create.

---

## Organizing the Category Tree
The order of categories determines how they appear on your POS screen.

*   **Reordering:** Use the **nine-dot icon** on the left side of a category to drag and drop it into a new position.
*   **Hierarchy:** Use the **drop-down arrows** to expand a parent category and reorder the subcategories within it.
*   **Management Tools:** The interface displays the number of products assigned to each category and its current status. Use the **Pencil Icon** to edit existing settings.

---

## Allocating Products to Categories
Once your structure is built, you must assign your products. Products can belong to **one or more** categories.

### Assignment Methods

| Method | Best For | Process |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Product by Product** | Unique items or small inventories | Filter by website/Pixfizz Core category. Click the **POS Categories** cell for a specific product and select the desired category. |
| **Mass Assignment** | Large groups (e.g., Photo Prints) | Filter to show all relevant products. Use the **top navigation bar** to "Select All," then use the mass-assign tool to move them to a category simultaneously. |
| **Unassigned Filter** | Cleanup and auditing | Filter products by **"No POS Category"** to identify items that have been missed during setup. |

---

## Summary of Best Practices

*   **File Formats:** Always use **WebP** for category images to prevent POS lag.
*   **Navigation:** Use the **arrow icons** in the assignment view to drill down into specific subcategories.
*   **Visibility:** If a category isn't appearing in your POS, check the **Active/Inactive** toggle in the category settings.
*   **Usage:** These categories are utilized both for **Manual Orders** and the **Point of Sale** interface.
